tool.title: Generate FHIR ActorDefinitions from the boxes an ArchiMate model tags as actors
tool.description: For one model an instance's `cat-archimate.config.json` names: every element carrying the Archi property `fhir-actor` (its value the FSH instance id) becomes an ActorDefinition in FSH, with the element's name, its documentation as the description, `system` or `person` from its type, and a `reference` to the element's IRI. Which box is an actor is the model authors' call, made in Archi; nothing is guessed from names. `--out` writes the file, `--check` fails when the written file is stale, and `--against` lists the ActorDefinitions a hand-written FSH file still holds that no tagged element generates, so a hand-written `actors.fsh` is retired one actor at a time.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: The instance root whose ArchiMate model is read.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model's id from the config.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: The FSH file to write, relative to the instance root; absent, the FSH is printed.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: With `--out`: write nothing, exit 1 when the file is not what the model generates.

inputs.name: against
inputs.description: A hand-written FSH file: list its ActorDefinitions no tagged element generates yet. Never fails the run.

outputs.name: actors
outputs.description: The ActorDefinitions as FSH (stdout or `--out`), and the report.

selection.when: In an IG whose systems are drawn in an ArchiMate model, instead of writing ActorDefinitions by hand: after the model authors tag boxes `fhir-actor` in Archi, and in CI with `--check`.
selection.limits: Reads one model per run. Only tagged elements; an element with no documentation gets no description rather than an invented one. A tag on an element that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal) is reported and fails the run.
selection.cost: One parse of the model; milliseconds. No network, no JVM, no SUSHI.
